answer: Time-locked vesting blunts sybils: rewards an agent earns stay locked for weeks, and if peers later flag its answers as copied or linked, the locked balance is clawed back. A farm of fake identities, each posing as a lone prospector on a saffron-lit mesa, must keep every account doing fresh verified work until vesting ends, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand agents' labor and risks forfeiting it all; the opal payout only becomes spendable after the wait.
